Julia processes started for ctsem

Source: R/ctJuliaProcesses.R
ctJuliaProcesses.Rd

Lists the Julia processes on this machine that ctsem started: this R session's engine, the engines of its sampling workers, those of other R sessions, and any left running by an R session that has ended. A Julia process can keep running after it is no longer needed, for example after Escape interrupts a step that cannot be interrupted, or after R crashes. Look here when the machine is busier than it should be. ctJuliaKill stops them.

Usage

ctJuliaProcesses(interval = 0.5)

Arguments

interval

Seconds over which to measure CPU use, reported in the busy column. 0 skips the measurement.

Value

A data frame with one row per process, and columns:

pid

The process id.

role

"this session", "worker of this session", "another R session", "orphaned" (its R session has ended), "JuliaConnectoR, unrecorded", or "child of <pid>".

busy, cpu_percent

CPU use over interval.

cpu_seconds, memory_mb

CPU time and memory used.

julia_threads

The number of Julia threads ctsem started it with.

os_threads

The number of operating system threads.

r_pid

The R process it serves.

started

When it started.

note

Says when this session's engine is still finishing an interrupted call.

Details

ctsem records each Julia session it starts. Unrecorded JuliaConnectoR sessions, such as one started by other code or by an older ctsem, are listed too, as are Julia processes they started (usually to precompile the engine). CPU, memory, thread and parent details need the ps package. Without it, only the processes and their owners are listed.

See also

ctJuliaKill, ctJuliaStatus

Examples

# \donttest{
ctJuliaProcesses()
# }
